Step 01 The cast
request and result Broadcast hardware connection

  1. Step 01

    The cast

    One Server owns the instrument. It is the only process holding a connection to the hardware, and everyone else in the picture is a consumer: your script, a colleague's session in the next room, the Server's own GUI, a Listener feeding a dashboard.

    They all reach the instrument the same way, whether they run on this machine or across the network.

  2. Step 02

    You make a request

    You call generator.frequency(5e9). Your generator is a Proxy Instrument, so nothing is set locally. The call is packed into a request and sent to the Server.

  3. Step 03

    The Server does the work

    The Server finds the real instrument, takes that instrument's lock, and runs the set on the driver that owns the hardware connection.

    While it holds the lock, nobody else's call to that instrument can interleave with yours.

  4. Step 04

    The answer comes back

    The result travels back to the client that asked, and only to that client.

    Every get you make is this same round trip. That is why a Proxy is never stale: it has no stored value to hand you, so it always goes and asks.

  5. Step 05

    The Server announces it

    The Server also announces the change to nobody in particular. That announcement is a Broadcast: published once, delivered to every subscriber.

  6. Step 06

    The watchers update

    The GUI redraws and the Listener records. They need the Broadcast because they hold a copy of the value, and a copy can go stale.

    Your colleague's session does not need it. It holds a Proxy, so the next time it asks it gets the new value anyway.
